title: Long March: Restart
credit_line: Artwork courtesy of M+ Sigg Collection, Hong Kong. By donation.
brief_description:
Feng Mengbo transforms one of modern China’s defining political stories into a playable artwork.

This interactive adventure is inspired by the Long March, the Chinese Red Army’s military retreat of 1934–36. It unfolds as a side-scrolling videogame artwork across two giant screens. A Red Army soldier travels through an 8-bit world inspired by historical landmarks and retro games like Street Fighter II and Super Mario Bros. Armed with exploding Coca-Cola cans, he fights iconic characters, aliens and armies as revolutionary history and global pop culture collide.

Feng first imagined Long March: Restart in 1994 as a series of paintings. It took 14 years before custom software could support the interactive version completed in 2008. The title’s “restart” suggests both a videogame mechanic and a return to history. By remixing communist and capitalist symbols with videogame references, Feng asks how history is constructed, retold and replayed through the images and systems that surround us.

Play along, or watch as the soldier advances, and join the surreal, pixelated march through time and space.
